# Sirach Chapter 34 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 34 | **Agents Consulted:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 34 moves through four major arguments: (1) the worthlessness of dreams and divination as sources of wisdom (vv. 1–8); (2) the value of experience and travel as the real teacher (vv. 9–13); (3) the security of those who fear the Lord (vv. 14–17); and (4) the worthlessness of sacrifice when paired with injustice toward the poor (vv. 18–26). Verses 20–22 are among Ben Sira's sharpest social critiques: stealing from the poor is explicitly equated with bloodshed. The purification image in vv. 25–26 is a masterstroke of ironic analogy: ritual washings repeated while the defilement continues are pointless, as is fasting while continuing to sin.

---

34:1 Empty and false hopes belong to the senseless, and dreams give wings to fools.

34:2 Like one who grasps at a shadow or chases the wind is anyone who gives heed to dreams.

34:3 What is seen in a dream is nothing but a reflection — the image of a face looking at a face.

34:4 From an unclean thing, what can be made clean? And from what is false, what can be true?

34:5 Divinations and omens and dreams are empty, and the heart fantasizes like a woman in labor.

34:6 Unless they are sent as a visitation from the Most High, give them no attention.

34:7 For dreams have led many astray, and those who set their hope in them have come to ruin.

34:8 The law will be fulfilled without falsehood, and wisdom is made complete in the mouth of the trustworthy.

34:9 A well-traveled man knows many things, and one with broad experience speaks with understanding.

34:10 One who has no experience knows little, but one who has traveled acquires great insight.

34:11 In my travels I have seen many things, and I understand more than I can put into words.

34:12 Many times I was in mortal danger, but I was rescued through these very experiences.

34:13 The spirit of those who fear the Lord will live, for their hope is in the one who saves them.

34:14 Whoever fears the Lord will not be afraid and will not play the coward, for he is their hope.

34:15 Blessed is the soul of the one who fears the Lord! On whom does he rely, and who is his support?

34:16 The eyes of the Lord watch over those who love him — a mighty shield and strong support, a shelter from the burning wind and shade from the noonday sun, a guard against stumbling and a defense against falling.

34:17 He lifts the spirit and makes the eyes shine; he gives healing, life, and blessing.

34:18 If someone sacrifices from what has been wrongly obtained, the offering is blemished, and the gifts of the lawless are not acceptable.

34:19 The Most High takes no pleasure in the offerings of the ungodly, nor is he appeased for sins by a multitude of sacrifices.

34:20 Like one who kills a son before his father's eyes is the man who brings a sacrifice from the property of the poor.

34:21 The bread of the needy is their life; whoever withholds it is a killer.

34:22 Depriving a neighbor of his living is murder, and withholding wages from a hired worker is bloodshed.

34:23 When one builds and another tears down, what have they gained but hard labor?

34:24 When one prays and another curses, whose voice will the Lord hear?

34:25 If someone washes after touching a corpse and then touches it again, what has the washing accomplished?

34:26 So it is with the man who fasts for his sins and then goes out and does the same things again: who will hear his prayer, and what has he gained by his self-humiliation?
